sections.h2: Who do you call about property tax in Dakota County, Minnesota?
sections.html:
Two county groups split the work. Assessing Services sets value and classification (651-438-4200), and Property Taxation & Records bills, collects and handles delinquent years (651-438-4576). Walk-in service for both is at the Administration Center in Hastings, the county seat, at 1590 Highway 55.

Dakota County is the third most populous county in Minnesota, at about 457,710 people on the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate. The Minnesota and Mississippi Rivers form its northern and eastern edge, and Lakeville is its largest city.

sections.h2: What do sellers face in Dakota County's housing market?
sections.html:
Dakota County mixes dense suburbs in the north with farmland and small towns in the south. Burnsville, Eagan, Apple Valley, Lakeville, Rosemount and Hastings sit among the larger cities, while Farmington, Hampton, Randolph and Miesville keep an older street grid. Wikipedia reports that 54% of residents work outside the county, mostly in the Twin Cities core.

  • School districts include 196 (Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan), 191 (Burnsville-Eagan-Savage), 194 (Lakeville), 197 (West St. Paul-Mendota Heights-Eagan), 200 (Hastings) and Special School District 6 (South St. Paul).
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes is $381,000 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Median household income is $106,318, and median gross rent is $1,548.
  • Owner-occupied housing is 74.9% of the stock, and 185,931 housing units were counted in July 2025.

A higher home value usually means a bigger property tax bill, so a seller should read the statement before pricing. The county's Tax Estimator page lets you test a number.

sections.h2: When is property tax due in Dakota County?
sections.html:
Real property tax is due May 15 and October 15, and both 2026 dates have passed. Agricultural land and manufactured homes have a November 16 second-half date, which is tomorrow, since November 15 falls on a Sunday this year.

Dakota County property tax due dates by property type (Property Taxation and Records)
Property typeFirst halfSecond half
Real propertyMay 15Oct. 15
Manufactured homeAug. 31Nov. 16
AgriculturalMay 15Nov. 16
Personal propertyMay 15none
Personal property on government-owned landMay 15Oct. 15

A payment mailed to the county must be postmarked on or before the due date or penalties apply. Under Minnesota Statutes section 279.01, homestead tax pays 2% after the due date and non-homestead 4%.

sections.h2: How can you pay Dakota County property tax?
sections.html:
The county lists five ways to pay, and each has its own cost.

  • Online or by phone through Paymentus (1-844-797-9075): cards carry a 2.29% convenience fee, Visa debit a $2.95 fee, and a bank transfer $0.35. Each transaction is capped at $100,000.
  • In person at the Administration Center in Hastings, the Northern Service Center in West St. Paul, or the Western Service Center in Apple Valley, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. weekdays, with a 2.49% fee on cards.
  • By mail to Property Taxation & Records, Attn: Taxation, 1590 Highway 55, Hastings, MN 55033-2343.
  • Automatic withdrawal, free, for owners whose lender does not pay the tax and who have no overdue tax. Forms filed now apply to taxes due in 2027, and a cancellation is due 15 days before a due date.

You can look up what you owe in the Property Information Search by entering only your house number.

sections.h2: What happens when Dakota County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Tax unpaid on January 2 becomes delinquent and monthly interest is added. A judgment, which is a tax lien, is entered against the property, owners get a letter in March, and a list of delinquent parcels is published in a local newspaper for two weeks.

The owner then has three years to pay in full or set up a payment plan. If the balance is still open after that, the property forfeits to the State of Minnesota, and the county manages it for the state. For parcels with 2022 or earlier tax unpaid, the sheriff served notice in June 2026 and the pay-or-plan date was August 31, 2026.

Penalty abatement is possible but narrow. The county considers clerical error, hardship such as a death or serious illness, a government-declared emergency, a postal error admitted in writing, and a stop-payment on a lost check made within 30 days. It does not accept a missing statement, a late payment alone, or general financial hardship.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Dakota County value?
sections.html:
For 2026 values the informal route and the county board are closed. The Special County Board of Appeal and Equalization met June 8, 2026, and after it adjourned Assessing Services could no longer change a 2026 value, so any change now applies to the 2027 assessment for taxes payable in 2028.

A petition to the Minnesota Tax Court is the formal option left. Section 278.01 requires a copy to be served on the county auditor and the petition and proof of service filed with the court administrator by April 30 of the year the tax is payable. Dakota County accepts email service at taxpetitions@co.dakota.mn.us, and it advises filing early because the county emails back an acknowledgment that must be filed with the court. Bring recent appraisals or sales of similar homes as evidence, and call the Tax Court at 651-539-3260 with questions.

sections.h2: Which Dakota County relief programs have filing dates?
sections.html:
The county's Home and Property page groups its relief programs together, and its 2026 date list gives a deadline for most of them. Missing one usually means waiting a full year.

  • Homestead, for owners who live in the house, with applications due December 31, 2026.
  • Blind and disabled homestead (Class 1b), due October 1.
  • Green Acres, due May 1, and Agricultural Preserves, due June 1.
  • Senior citizen property tax deferment, disabled veterans, open spaces and property tax exemption, plus state property tax refunds and local option disaster abatement.

The 2026 open book appeal ran March 11 to May 1, and manufactured home homestead applications were due May 29. The county also posts proposed taxes for 2027 on its Home and Property page.

sections.h2: What does the tax do at a Dakota County closing?
sections.html:
The county notes that cities and townships set their own sale rules, especially for wells, septic systems, manufactured homes and owners on Medical Assistance, whose certificate of clearance line is 651-554-6555. Under section 272.12, the county auditor must confirm there is no delinquent tax before a deed is recorded, and Dakota County says it can return a deed for delinquent tax.

Home buyers should also watch the calendar for programs. Homestead applications are due December 31, 2026, and the Blind or Disabled Class 1b applications were due October 1. Open Space applications are due November 3.

faqs.q: What is the next Dakota County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: November 16, 2026, for agricultural property and manufactured homes, since November 15 is a Sunday. Real property was due May 15 and October 15. Homestead applications are due December 31.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Dakota County value?
faqs.a: Only through the Minnesota Tax Court. The county board met on June 8, 2026, so Assessing Services can change only the 2027 assessment. A petition for taxes payable in 2027 is due by April 30, 2027.

faqs.q: How do I pay Dakota County property tax by phone?
faqs.a: Call 1-844-797-9075 and use a Discover, MasterCard or Visa card at 2.29%, a Visa debit at $2.95, or a bank transfer at $0.35. Your payment is complete only once you get a confirmation number.

faqs.q: How long before Dakota County can take a property for unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Owners have three years from the delinquency to pay or set up a payment plan before the property forfeits to the state. Interest builds monthly in that time. Call 651-438-4576 about your parcel.

faqs.q: Does Dakota County give a free way to check my balance?
faqs.a: Yes. The Property Information Search is free, and you enter only your house number to see what you owe. Property Taxation & Records can help at taxation@co.dakota.mn.us or 651-438-4576, and the county also offers a free paperless notice option that sends your statement by email.
